info.title: BigBooks API
info.description: All endpoints require a bearer JWT issued by the BigBooks authorization server. Many endpoints additionally take an X-Acting-Party-ID header selecting the tenant party being acted for. Mutations of versioned resources require an If-Match header echoing the ETag from the resource's GET. List endpoints paginate with page_size and page_number (zero-based). Full conventions and a domain glossary: https://staging.bigbooks.app/api/docs/integrator-guide.md

current.description: Balance from posted entries, in the account's own currency and sign convention: an asset's is what it holds and a liability's what is owed, both positive in the ordinary case. A negative asset balance is an overdraft, a negative liability balance a credit.

available.description: current plus pending entries, in the same currency and sign convention.

rates.description: Every exchange rate applied, for disclosure alongside the converted figures.

count.description: Records included in the converted figures. Excludes unconvertedUnitTypes records.

unitType.description: Target unit type the grand total is expressed in.

unconvertedUnitTypes.description: Unit types with no available rate. Their subtotals appear only in `totals`, unconverted — never silently included or dropped.

balance.description: The account's running balance after this entry, in the account's own sign convention (a liability's is what is owed, positive in the ordinary case). Present on account-register rows only; null elsewhere.

signedAmount.description: amount as a change to the account's balance in its own sign convention: positive grows what an asset holds or what a liability owes.

count.description: Number of records matching the filters, across all pages.

unitType.description: Unit type (currency) these totals are denominated in. Totals in different unit types are never combined.

moneyIn.description: Total of positive (inflow) amounts across all matching records.

moneyOut.description: Total of negative (outflow) amounts across all matching records, as a positive number.

netAmount.description: Signed net of all matching amounts: moneyIn - moneyOut.

latestDate.description: Latest record date in the matching set.

earliestDate.description: Earliest record date in the matching set.

rate.description: Exchange rate applied: 1 unit of unitType = rate units of the target.

unitType.description: Unit type that was converted into the target.

asOfDate.description: Publication date of the applied rate.

forexSource.description: Rate source, e.g. ECB daily reference rates.

entries.description: Primary accounting entries (debits/credits) matching query. Null when not included.

offsets.description: Offsetting entries that balance the transactions. Null when not included.

parties.description: Parties that own the accounts. Null when not included.

accounts.description: Accounts involved in entries. Null when not included.

journals.description: Journals (transactions) containing entries. Null when not included.

entrySetTotals.description: Server-computed totals per unit type across ALL records matching the filters — not just this page. Use these figures for any total, count, or date span; never sum page rows. Null when not included.

key.description: A name for the account within this body, so a mortgage can name the house securing it before either is saved: 'house', 'mortgage'. Any string unique among the body's accounts, never stored; to resend a saved scenario, use each account's id as its key and a loan's collateralId as its collateral.

name.description: What the account is, in the user's words: 'Lake house', 'Lake house mortgage'.

accountType.description: ASSET (a house, a car, a rental, a brokerage account) or LIABILITY (the loan on it).

assetType.description: For an ASSET: what kind, as a book account's assetType — BROKERAGE, IRA, _401K, SAVINGS, FIXED_ASSET. An investment account with no appreciationRate grows by the party's assumed return, as a book one does; anything else grows only by its appreciationRate or a GROWTH. It also says how money leaving the account is taxed, as a book account's does: an IRA or a 401(k) is tax-deferred (see the scenario's taxRate) and can carry an RMD.

openingBalance.description: An asset's value or a liability's principal on the day it appears.

openDate.description: The day the account appears: the purchase, the loan's origination. Once it has passed, a run opens the account on the run's first day instead, the loan originating then.

fundedFromAccountId.description: The book account the down payment leaves on the open date.

fundedAmount.description: The down payment, leaving fundedFromAccountId on the open date.

appreciationRate.description: An asset's appreciation, percent a year, compounded monthly; omit for none.

apr.description: A liability's annual percentage rate; with termMonths, the loan follows its amortization schedule from the open date.

escrow.description: Monthly escrow leaving the paying account with each payment; never reduces the loan.

paymentFromAccountId.description: The book account each scheduled payment, plus escrow, leaves.

disposedOn.description: The day an asset is sold or a liability paid off; after its openDate.

proceedsToAccountId.description: The book account the sale's proceeds (the asset's value less the loans it secures) land in, or a lone liability's payoff leaves.

collateral.description: For a liability: the key of the asset in this body securing it — the house under this mortgage. Several loans may name one asset; selling it pays them all off from the proceeds.

collateralAccountId.description: For a liability: the book asset securing it, in place of collateral — the home already owned under a new HELOC. A DISPOSE that sells the asset pays it off from the proceeds.

horizonYears.description: How many years ahead the scenario runs, 1 to 60; default 30. Ignored when the horizon runs to a person's age.

horizonPersonId.description: The person whose age the horizon runs to — 'to age 95' — in place of a number of years.

horizonAge.description: The age the horizon runs to; default 95 when a person is named.

inflationRate.description: General inflation, percent a year, for every recurring bill on the calendar and every WITHDRAWAL without a rate of its own. Omit to inherit the party's planning assumptions.

returnRate.description: Annual return, percent, on every investment account without an undated GROWTH flow of its own. Omit to inherit.

incomeGrowthRate.description: Annual growth, percent, of every recurring deposit on the calendar — the paychecks. Omit to inherit.

taxRate.description: The household's effective income tax rate, percent (0 to 99), on money leaving a tax-deferred account — an IRA, a 401(k): a WITHDRAWAL or TRANSFER from one draws its tax on top of the amount, and an RMD is received less it. Omit to inherit; zero, the default, taxes nothing. A tax-deferred account is an asset — on the books, or a hypothetical one by the assetType it states — of assetType IRA, SEP_IRA, SIMPLE_IRA, SARSEP, KEOGH, _401A, _401K, _403B, _457B, PROFIT_SHARING_PLAN, PENSION, RETIREMENT, RRSP, RRIF, LIRA, LRSP, LIF, LRIF, RLIF, PRIF, SIPP, FIXED_ANNUITY, VARIABLE_ANNUITY or OTHER_ANNUITY. Nothing leaving any other account is taxed: not a tax-free one — ROTH, ROTH_401K, an HSA, a 529, a TFSA, an ISA — nor a taxable one, a brokerage or a depository account, whose basis and interest the books do not know.

volatility.description: The volatility of the investment return, percent a year (0 to 100) — the standard deviation of the market's return a simulation draws each month from, around the return. Omit to inherit; a run as stated ignores it.

flows.description: The assumptions. Replaces every existing flow on update, each saved again under a new id.

streamOverrides.description: The scenario's say over the calendar's streams: end a paycheck at retirement, drop a subscription, re-price a bill. Replaces the existing overrides on update, each saved again under a new id.

excludedAccountIds.description: Accounts left out of the run altogether. An excluded account cannot carry a flow, be a fallback or fund, pay or receive a hypothetical account's money; in a run with member scenarios, an account any of them counts on stays in. Replaces the existing exclusions on update.

items.description: Accounts left out of the run altogether. An excluded account cannot carry a flow, be a fallback or fund, pay or receive a hypothetical account's money; in a run with member scenarios, an account any of them counts on stays in. Replaces the existing exclusions on update.

memberScenarioIds.description: Scenarios of the party's member parties to run together with this one — a business's plan under a household's. At most one per member party. Replaces the existing members on update.

items.description: Scenarios of the party's member parties to run together with this one — a business's plan under a household's. At most one per member party. Replaces the existing members on update.

accounts.description: Accounts that exist only in this scenario's run — the house not yet bought and its mortgage, the next car — each appearing on its open date and, if sold or paid off, disposed of on a date. Replaces the existing ones on update, each saved again under a new id.

key.description: A name for the flow within this body, so another flow can refer to it before either is saved: the CONTRIBUTION an employer match names as matchOf. Any string unique among the body's flows, never stored; to resend a saved scenario, use each flow's id as its key and the match's matchOfFlowId as its matchOf.

flowType.description: What the flow does. An RMD is the required minimum distribution from a tax-deferred account (see the scenario's taxRate): it names the account as accountId or hypotheticalAccount, its owner as personId — required — and, optionally, where the money lands as targetAccountId or hypotheticalTargetAccount, an asset or a liability; without one the money leaves the household's accounts. The rule sets the rest: from the year the owner reaches the required age — 72 if born before 1951, 73 if born before 1960, 75 after, read from their birth date — each January 1 the account's balance as the year opens, over the IRS uniform lifetime divisor at their age at the year's end, leaves the account, received less the scenario's taxRate. An RMD states no amount, percent, rate, cadenceMonths, startDate, endDate, startAge or endAge; sending any of them is a 400, as is an account that is not tax-deferred.

accountId.description: The book account the flow acts on: the funding account of a withdrawal, the destination of a contribution (an asset that receives a deposit, or a liability that receives an extra payment), the source of a transfer, the account that grows or is shocked, the expense or revenue category of a SPENDING flow, the asset sold or the liability paid off by a DISPOSE, the tax-deferred account an RMD distributes from. Give this or hypotheticalAccount, one of them.

hypotheticalAccount.description: In place of accountId: the key of a hypothetical account in this body the flow acts on — extra principal paid into the mortgage of the house not yet bought, a monthly contribution into a brokerage account opened later, the growth of that account. Money moves through it only while the account exists — from its open date until it is disposed of: an occurrence outside that does not happen, on either side, and the flow keeps its own days and growth. A GROWTH only on an account neither appreciating nor on loan terms, which grow it already. Not for SPENDING, whose account is a category, nor DISPOSE: a hypothetical account is sold or paid off on its own disposedOn.

targetAccountId.description: The other side, when there is one: where a contribution comes from, where a withdrawal or transfer goes, the account a SPENDING category is paid from, the account a DISPOSE's proceeds land in or its payoff leaves, where an RMD lands. Required for TRANSFER, as this or hypotheticalTargetAccount, and for SPENDING and DISPOSE, as this.

hypotheticalTargetAccount.description: In place of targetAccountId: the key of a hypothetical account in this body on the other side — where a withdrawal or transfer lands, what a contribution is paid from. Not for SPENDING or DISPOSE, whose other side is a book account.

label.description: What the flow is, in the user's words: 'Emma's tuition', 'retirement living expenses'.

amount.description: Per occurrence for recurring flows; signed for ONE_TIME, positive being money in; the category's new monthly amount for SPENDING; the balance to reach for TARGET; for a DISPOSE of an asset, the price it fetches — omit to sell at its projected balance. Money into a liability pays it down. Not used by GROWTH, SHOCK or RMD, nor by a match, whose percent says how much.

startDate.description: First occurrence for recurring flows; the day for ONE_TIME, SHOCK and DISPOSE; the first month for SPENDING; the date to reach the balance by for TARGET; for GROWTH, the first day the rate applies — omit for the whole run. A dated GROWTH replaces the undated one, or the assumed return, while it is in force: a lean decade is a GROWTH at the lean rate between two dates, and the usual rate resumes after it. A DISPOSE whose day has passed happens on the run's first day instead.

endDate.description: Last occurrence for recurring flows and SPENDING, or the last day a GROWTH applies; omit to run to the horizon.

cadenceMonths.description: Months between occurrences of a recurring flow: 1 monthly, 12 yearly. SPENDING is always monthly; a match follows the flow it matches.

rate.description: A percentage: the annual return for GROWTH, the annual growth of the amount for recurring flows (tuition inflation, a raise) and SPENDING, the change for a SHOCK (-30 for a 30% fall), the growth of a match's ceiling. A WITHDRAWAL or an expense SPENDING without one grows by the scenario's inflation, a revenue SPENDING by its income growth; send 0 for none.

percent.description: A WITHDRAWAL stated as the share of the account's balance drawn per year — 4 for the 4% rule — in place of an amount; each occurrence takes the year's share spread over the year's occurrences, so a monthly draw takes a twelfth. For a match: the share of the matched flow's amount the match adds — 50 for a half match.

floorAmount.description: The least a percent WITHDRAWAL draws per occurrence, in today's money, growing by the rate: a guardrail under lean years.

ceilingAmount.description: The most a percent WITHDRAWAL draws per occurrence, in today's money, growing by the rate: a guardrail over strong years. For a match: the most it adds per occurrence — the employer's cap, 6% of the salary — growing by the rate, or by the matched flow's when the match has none.

fallbackAccountIds.description: Accounts a WITHDRAWAL draws on once its own runs dry, in order: the taxable brokerage first, then the IRA, then the Roth. The last takes whatever is left.

items.description: Accounts a WITHDRAWAL draws on once its own runs dry, in order: the taxable brokerage first, then the IRA, then the Roth. The last takes whatever is left.

personId.description: The person whose ages date the flow, when startAge or endAge is given in place of a date. Required for an RMD: the account's owner, whose birth date sets the year the distributions begin and each year's divisor.

startAge.description: The person's age on the first occurrence — 'from age 62' — in place of startDate; resolved from their birth date when the scenario runs.

endAge.description: The person's age on the last occurrence — 'until 70' — in place of endDate.

matchOf.description: For a CONTRIBUTION that matches another — the employer's share of a 401(k) contribution: the key of the CONTRIBUTION in this body it matches. The match fires whenever that flow does, adding percent of its amount, at most ceilingAmount; it has no amount, dates or cadence of its own.

accountId.description: The account the stream is on: the checking account a subscription is paid from, the card it is charged to, or the loan whose schedule this overrides. A payment a DISPOSE has moved onto another account may be named by either account: the one it was on, or the one it is on from the sale.

merchantName.description: The merchant of the recurring stream, as the calendar names it. Omit to override the account's loan schedule instead.

excluded.description: Drop the stream from the run altogether — from startDate or startAge on, when the override has one.

startDate.description: First day the override is in force: the raise that starts in March, the rent that goes up in January. Before it the stream runs as the books have it, or as an earlier override on the same stream says. Omit for an override in force from the run's first day; a stream may have several overrides with different starts, and at most one without.

endDate.description: Last day the stream fires: a subscription cancelled, a paycheck that stops at retirement. Ending a loan's schedule stops its payments and every stream paying it, the balance still owed; ending a stream that pays a loan stops that stream, and the loan is paid down by what still pays it. onTrack.description: True when the projection meets the target. For a hypothetical account not open on the date (plannedOpenDate): never for an asset, which holds nothing then; always for a liability, which owes nothing then.

gap.description: How far the projection misses the target, always positive; absent when on track, or when the account is not yet open on the date.

plannedOpenDate.description: The hypothetical account's openDate, when it is not open on the target's date — it opens later, or never, as when the account funding its purchase is closed first. Nothing is held or owed on it then: an asset's target is not met — move the date or the openDate, or fund the purchase — while a liability's is.

requiredMonthlyContribution.description: The extra contribution, every month from next month — or from the day the account opens, for one not yet open — until the date, that would reach the target; absent when on track or when there is no month to save in.

contributionAccountId.description: The account requiredMonthlyContribution is paid into: this account, or — when the scenario closes it into another before the date — the account its money is in by then, whose balance answers for the target. Absent with the contribution.

id.description: The flow, account or liability behind the events, when there is one.

label.description: The merchant of a recurring stream, the label of a flow, the name of an account.

amount.description: The events' total, signed as the list holding it says: an attribution period's sources in the account's own sign convention, a cash-flow period's in cash direction.

baselineMonthly.description: What the category cost or brought the account each month over the trailing year, in the account's own sign convention; the part of the baseline the flow replaces.

monthly.description: The flow's monthly amount, as given.

monthsOfHistory.description: How many months of the funding account's history the baseline share is over, as for the account's own baseline.

PdfBankingFileParams.description: Page range and statement period bounding the extraction, as a JSON multipart part

CsvBankingFileParams.description: Sampling options and the account whose saved column mappings are returned, as a JSON multipart part

persona.description: The system prompt BigBooks maintains to run under, rendered for the caller at request time: BOOKKEEPER (factual, the default) or ADVISOR (personal-finance advice; the digest persona). Mutually exclusive with systemContent.

systemContent.description: A system prompt of your own in place of a persona. Prefer a persona: the rendered prompts carry the coded-label rules the aliasing layer depends on, and a prompt without them produces mangled names.

persona.description: The system prompt BigBooks maintains for the conversation, rendered for the caller when it starts: BOOKKEEPER (factual, the default) or ADVISOR (personal-finance advice). Mutually exclusive with systemContent.

systemContent.description: A system prompt of your own in place of a persona. Prefer a persona: the rendered prompts carry the coded-label rules the aliasing layer depends on, and a prompt without them produces mangled names.

date.description: When the item is expected. A date in the past means it is expected but has not been seen yet.

unitType.description: Unit type of the account; the amount is native to it.

amount.description: Expected signed change to the account's balance, in the account's own sign convention — positive means more held in an asset or more owed on a liability: a paycheck into checking and a charge on a card are positive, a bill paid from checking is negative. For a loan payment, the principal portion alone, negative since it lowers what is owed.

confidence.description: The recurrence model's score for its verdict; absent for a heuristic verdict and for loan payments.

windowDays.description: Spread of the stream's past gaps in days: how far from the date the charge tends to land. Absent for loan payments.

interest.description: Interest portion of a loan payment; absent for recurrences.

escrow.description: Escrow the lender collects with a loan payment, when the liability carries an escrow term; absent for recurrences.

paymentDue.description: The full amount due on a loan payment: principal, interest and escrow. Absent for recurrences, whose amount is the whole charge.

plannedTransactionId.description: The planned transaction this is one side of; absent for recurrences and loan payments.

label.description: The planned transaction's label, in the user's words; absent for recurrences and loan payments.

unitType.description: Target unit type the total is expressed in.

transactionCount.description: Transactions behind the converted total; excludes unconvertedUnitTypes rows.

rates.description: Every exchange rate applied. Empty when every row is already in the target.

unconvertedUnitTypes.description: Unit types with no rate as of the period's close; their rows appear only in statistics, unconverted.

statistics.description: One row per category and native unit type. Means, medians and deviations are native to that unit type and are never converted.

convertedTotals.description: Per category on this page, the total amount folded into the target unit type with the rates applied. Always disclose the rates and any unconverted unit types when presenting these.

statistics.description: One row per unit type the merchant was paid in during the period; amounts are native to that unit type and are never converted.

minAmount.description: The smallest transaction amount in the period, in cash direction: money out negative — so the largest purchase — and a refund positive, whether paid from a bank account or charged to a card.

maxAmount.description: The largest transaction amount in the period, in cash direction: the smallest purchase, or a refund.

meanAmount.description: The mean transaction amount in the period, in cash direction: negative for spending, whether paid from a bank account or charged to a card.

low.description: The 10th percentile across the paths: nine paths in ten did at least this well.

high.description: The 90th percentile across the paths: one path in ten did better.

paths.description: How many paths the market took.

seed.description: The seed the paths were drawn from: the same seed, scenarios, books and settings draw the same paths again.

unreachableAccountIds.description: Accounts a scenario names on the books of a party its own party no longer reaches, left out of the run with the flows on them.

items.description: Accounts a scenario names on the books of a party its own party no longer reaches, left out of the run with the flows on them.

assumptions.description: The rates each party's books ran under, the volatility among them, and where each came from.

marketAccountIds.description: The investment accounts whose growth the market moved; every other account grew as stated on every path.

items.description: The investment accounts whose growth the market moved; every other account grew as stated on every path.

successPercent.description: The share of paths, percent, on which every funding account covered its withdrawals; absent when the scenarios draw no withdrawals, there being nothing to fund.

funding.description: One entry per account that funds withdrawals: how often it is funded, and the typical shortfall when it is not.

targets.description: Every TARGET flow: how often the paths reach it, and the band the balance lands in on its date.

accounts.description: Every asset and liability account in scope, its balance band on every sampled day.

netPositions.description: Assets minus liabilities per unit type, unconverted, as a band on every sampled day.

hypothetical.description: True for a scenario's hypothetical account, planned rather than on the books.

opening.description: Balance before the first day's flows, the same on every path.

belowZeroPercent.description: The share of paths, percent, on which the balance fell below zero on any day — an overdraft on an asset, a credit balance on a liability.

points.description: The balance's 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles across the paths every step days from the first day, and on the last day whatever the step; the last point is the closing band.

withdrawals.description: The withdrawals this account funds, by label.

items.description: The withdrawals this account funds, by label.

fundedPercent.description: The share of paths, percent, on which every account the withdrawals draw on stays at or above zero and every withdrawal has an account to draw on — the run's own funded verdict, path by path.

medianShortDate.description: Among the paths that fall short, the median of the first day a withdrawal cannot be covered; absent when none falls short.

medianShortfall.description: Among the paths that fall short, the median shortfall, as a negative number; absent when none falls short.

target.description: The balance to hold by the date — or, for a liability, to owe no more than.

onTrackPercent.description: The share of paths, percent, on which the balance projected on the date meets the target.

projected.description: The balance projected on the date across the paths — of the account, or of the one a scenario closed it into by then.

plannedOpenDate.description: The hypothetical account's openDate when it is not open on the target's date, on every path alike: an asset's target is then never met, a liability's always.

fromDate.description: The run's first day, from which the balances are projected.

hypothetical.description: True when the account is a scenario's hypothetical account, planned rather than on the books.

opening.description: The balance on the morning of the window's first day.

closing.description: The balance at the end of the window's last day.

amount.description: The change to the balance, in the account's own sign convention — positive means more held in an asset or more owed on a liability.

accountId.description: The account's id in this run, or in the first run for an account only it has; for a hypothetical account, the id of whichever run supplied it.

hypothetical.description: True for a scenario's hypothetical account, matched to the first run's by name and unit type rather than by id.
True for a scenario's hypothetical account, planned rather than on the books; runs match one by its name, its id being each scenario's own.

netPositions.description: This run's net position less the first run's, per unit type, on every sampled day; zero in a run with no account in the unit type.

key.description: The scenario's name, with the variant when there is one: 'Retire at 62 · return 4%'.

unreachableAccountIds.description: Accounts the scenario names on the books of a party its own party no longer reaches, left out of the run with the flows on them.

items.description: Accounts the scenario names on the books of a party its own party no longer reaches, left out of the run with the flows on them.

source.description: Where the recurrence verdict came from: the cadence HEURISTIC, the recurrence MODEL, or the party's declaration (DECLARED).

confidence.description: The model's score for its verdict; absent for a heuristic or declared verdict.

declarationId.description: The declaration the row rests on when its source is DECLARED; withdraw it to take the word back.

nextExpectedDate.description: When the next charge is expected: the last one plus the median gap, or plus the declared frequency's nominal gap. A date in the past means it is expected but has not been seen yet.

previousAmount.description: PRICE_CHANGE: the mean charge before the change.

changePercent.description: PRICE_CHANGE: percentage change in the charge's size; positive is an increase.

changedOn.description: PRICE_CHANGE: first charge at the new amount.

expectedOn.description: LAPSED: when the next charge had been expected.

accounts.description: DUPLICATE: every account the merchant bills, this one included.

sigmas.description: Standard deviations from the category mean an amount had to reach to be listed.

minimumCount.description: Transactions a category needed in the baseline year before its amounts were judged at all.

truncated.description: true when the range held more journals than were scanned; the newest were judged, so narrow the dates to reach the older ones.

accountId.description: The expense or revenue account the amount was compared against.

amount.description: The category-side amount, signed in the account's own convention: a refund on an expense category is negative.

mean.description: Mean transaction amount for the category over the baseline year.

stddev.description: Standard deviation of the category's transaction amounts over the baseline year.

transactionCount.description: How many transactions the baseline rests on.

periodDate.description: First day of the baseline year.

rates.description: Every exchange rate applied, for disclosure alongside the converted amount.

unitType.description: Target unit type the converted amount is expressed in.

unconvertedUnitTypes.description: Unit types with no available rate. Their amounts appear only in their own per-unit-type entries, unconverted — never silently included or dropped.

valueTotals.description: Market value totals per unit type across ALL listed holdings. Values in different unit types are never summed together; use these instead of summing rows.

costBasisTotals.description: Cost-basis totals per unit type across the holdings that report one.

unitType.description: Unit type the price, value, cost basis and gain are denominated in; nothing here is converted.
Unit type (currency) the amount is denominated in.
Target unit type every headline figure is expressed in.

rates.description: Every exchange rate applied to fold the native figures into the target. Empty when every account is already in the target. Always disclose these alongside the headline figures.

unconvertedUnitTypes.description: Unit types with no rate as of the period's close. Their figures appear only in nativeFigures and are absent from the headline — say so.

nativeFigures.description: One unconverted set of figures per native unit type.

revenues.description: Revenue accounts with activity in the period, largest first.

expenses.description: Expense accounts with activity in the period, largest first.

unitType.description: Unit type every figure here is denominated in; nothing here is converted.

amount.description: The period's total: revenue earned, or expense incurred. A refund or reversal larger than the period's activity makes it negative.

baselines.description: Each cash account's everyday baseline the forecast spread over the days of each month, the slices summing to its monthlyNet; empty when the baseline was switched off or no cash account has everyday history.

netPositions.description: Assets minus liabilities per unit type, unconverted.

payoffDate.description: When the debt is cleared; absent when the strategy never clears it within fifty years.

extraPayment.description: The amount paid each month on top of every minimum.

months.description: Months until every debt is cleared; absent when a debt never clears within fifty years.

interestSaved.description: Interest this strategy saves compared with MINIMUM; zero for MINIMUM itself.

monthsSaved.description: Months sooner than MINIMUM every debt is cleared; absent when either never clears.

payoffs.description: The debts in the order they are cleared.

balances.description: Total owed at the end of each month.

apr.description: Annual percentage rate, as a percentage.

minimumPayment.description: The monthly payment the plan makes at least: the calculated amortization payment when the loan terms are known, otherwise the stated payment.

reason.description: What the account is missing: an APR, a payment, or a balance to pay down.

unitType.description: Target unit type inflow and outflow are expressed in.

rates.description: Every exchange rate applied to fold the native flows into the target, as of the period's end. Empty when every flow is already in the target.

unconvertedUnitTypes.description: Unit types with no rate for the period; their flows appear only in nativeFlows and are absent from inflow and outflow — say so.

nativeFlows.description: Each currency's own inflow and outflow for the period, unconverted.

unitType.description: Target unit type every period's inflow and outflow are expressed in.
Unit type this inflow and outflow are denominated in; nothing here is converted.

budgets.description: Budgets matching query. Null when not included.

month.description: The first day of the month projected.

monthEnd.description: The last day of the month projected.

postedThrough.description: The last day whose postings the actuals hold: today, or the month's last day once it is over. Absent for a month not begun.

daysRemaining.description: The days after postedThrough still to come in the month: the days the remaining figures cover.

monthsOfHistory.description: The months of history behind the everyday run-rate: the trailing year, or the age of the oldest cash account when it is younger.

categories.description: One row per category with anything to say — a posting, a stream still to come, an everyday share or a budget — in its own unit type.

totals.description: The rows added up per unit type and account type.

unitType.description: Unit type of the category; every figure here is native to it. Never add rows of different unit types together — use totals.

actualToDate.description: What has posted to the category from the first of the month through postedThrough; 0 for a month not begun. Signed as the budget reports are: spending positive on an expense, income positive on a revenue, so a refund larger than the month's spending makes an expense's figure negative.

remainingKnown.description: What the recurring streams dated in the days left land on the category, each at the share of it the stream's past journals put there; 0 for a month that is over. Signed as actualToDate is.

remainingEveryday.description: The category's share of the cash accounts' everyday activity — outside the recurring streams — for the days left, as its trailing monthly run-rate times the share of the month remaining; 0 for a month that is over. Signed as actualToDate is.

projected.description: Where the category ends the month: actualToDate plus remainingKnown plus remainingEveryday. Signed as actualToDate is: positive spending on an expense, positive income on a revenue.

budgeted.description: The month's budget for the category, the sum of its budget days; absent when none is set. Signed as actualToDate is: the spending allowed on an expense, positive; the income expected on a revenue, positive.

variance.description: budgeted less projected: positive on an expense is money left unspent, negative overspending; positive on a revenue is income still short of the budget, negative income beyond it. Absent without a budget.

actualToDate.description: The categories' actualToDate added up. Signed as the budget reports are: spending positive on an expense, income positive on a revenue, so a refund larger than the month's spending makes an expense's figure negative.

budgeted.description: The sum of the budgets set among these categories; absent when none has one.

unitType.description: Target unit type revenue and expense are expressed in.

revenues.description: Total across the period's REVENUE accounts, converted into the target.

expenses.description: Total across the period's EXPENSE accounts, converted into the target.

forexDisclosures.description: Every exchange rate applied to fold the native totals into the target, as of the period's end. Empty when every account is already in the target.

unconvertedUnitTypes.description: Unit types with no rate for the period; their totals appear only in nativeTotals and are absent from revenue and expense — say so.

nativeBudgetPeriodTotals.description: Each currency's own revenue and expense for the period, unconverted.

unitType.description: Target unit type every budgetPeriodTotals figure is expressed in.

budgetPeriods.description: One row per account and period, each in that account's own currency. Never add these together across accounts — use budgetPeriodTotals.

budgetPeriodTotals.description: Per-period totals across every budgeted account, converted into the target unit type with the rates applied disclosed. Always present; empty when there are no budgetPeriods.

unitType.description: Unit type this revenue and expense are denominated in; nothing here is converted.
Unit type every figure in this sheet is denominated in; nothing here is converted.

netWorth.description: Assets minus liabilities — net worth as of the date.

solvencyGap.description: Matched liabilities minus assets; positive means liabilities exceed assets (insolvent).

purchasePower.description: Cash on hand plus available credit — total immediately spendable.

netWorth.description: Assets minus liabilities — net worth as of the date.

solvencyGap.description: Matched liabilities minus assets; positive means liabilities exceed assets (insolvent).

purchasePower.description: Cash on hand plus available credit — total immediately spendable.

rates.description: Every exchange rate applied to fold the native sheets into the target. Empty when every account is already in the target. Always disclose these alongside the headline figures.

unconvertedUnitTypes.description: Unit types with no rate as of the date. Their sheets appear only in nativeSheets and are absent from the headline figures — say so.

nativeSheets.description: One unconverted sheet per native unit type; each balances on its own.
